data.description:
## Problem

When the proxy returns a 503 'All providers exhausted' response, retry_after is **hardcoded to 60 seconds**. The Worklog extension's retry loop then waits 2 seconds, retries, fails again, and loops for up to ~60 seconds with exponential backoff — all while real provider availability is **minutes to hours away** (big-pickle cooldown: 86400s; go-2 reset: Aug 30; deepseek: outside available_times).

This wastes time and produces repeated error notifications that confuse the user.

## Solution

The proxy already collects per-provider availability data in unavailable_providers (cooldown maps) and knows about available_times windows. Compute the **real next-available time** and emit it as:

1. **A Retry-After HTTP header** (standard mechanism, integer seconds until retry is valid)
2. **The retry_after field** in the JSON response (already exists but is wrong)

### Implementation details

The proxy response is built in proxy/proxy/provider.py -> _build_exhausted_response() (or wherever the 503 is constructed). Compute the real retry_after as:

  retry_after = max(
      max(unavailable_providers.values()) if unavailable_providers else 0,
      next_available_times_window_edge(),
      next_usage_limit_reset()
  )

### Acceptance Criteria

1. retry_after in the JSON 503 response reflects the **real** next provider availability (not hardcoded 60).
2. A Retry-After HTTP header is set on 503 responses with the same value.
3. The value is the maximum of: cooldown durations, available_times window edges, and usage-limit reset times.
4. If all providers are actually available (edge case), retry_after = 0.
5. Existing tests pass (update any that assert retry_after == 60).
6. Full test suite passes (quiet mode).

### Related work

This is the **proxy-side** half of the fix. The **extension-side** half (Worklog ContextHub) is tracked separately: the Worklog recovery module's classifyError must recognize 'All providers exhausted' and route it to the retry loop with this new Retry-After delay.
data.title: Honest Retry-After: emit real provider availability windows

Follow-up implementation for the KV slot save/restore reuse-gap evaluation (parent LP-0MTAQNB7J0094X71, evaluation-only per AC #5). Created by F5 (LP-0MTCMGJBM007AQ55).

Implements the F4/F5 selected fix set for both modes (fast 3 slots cap 83285 / cheap 2 slots cap 126976):

1. CAP RAISE/RESTORE-PATH FIX (dominant, ~22.8M prefill-tokens/day): ensure persistence applies at the routing clamp for oversized sessions (F2 root cause: 38/48 sessions gated out with 0 saves). Raise session_slot_max_prompt_tokens to per-slot clamp (fast 83285, cheap 126976 — pinned per LP-0MTBTCB8D000OQ0C) AND fix the restore path so accepted sessions actually restore (native checkpoint restores at 4.88%). MUST carry the GPU-wedge plan unchanged (LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO): timeout base 3.0s + 0.0015s/token, max 60s; cooldown 300s after 3 consecutive failures; skip-when-busy stays on.
2. AFFINITY/SLOT-OWNERSHIP FIX (~3.3M): lease churn (166 orphan + 141 evicted releases/day) breaks session-slot continuity (F2); orphan-cleanup continuity + LP-0MSB0RV72001KNRV registry-leak class.
3. RESTORE-BEFORE-SAVE ORDERING (~0.44M): restore before saving for hot same-slot sessions, zero GPU footprint change.
4. /slots 500 + slots_stale fix feeds affinity: router-mode GET /slots 500s (6,865/day, 100% router-proxied per F3) — direct model-instance polling / last-known-state fallback (F3 fix rank 1).

Reference the F1-F5 deliverables: docs/dev/save-restore-reuse-gap-root-cause.md, docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md, docs/dev/restore-rate-metric-fix-ranking.md, docs/dev/mode-specific-recommendation.md; scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py, slot_reuse_gap_analysis.py, slots_500_triage.py, restore_metric_fix_ranking.py, mode_recommendation.py.

## ACs

1. Fast mode serves oversized sessions (up to the 83285 clamp) with persistence: oversized-session save/restore events appear in the corpus for previously-gated sessions.
2. Cheap mode (cap 126976) likewise persists and restores.
3. Native checkpoint restore rate for >50K contexts improves measurably from the 8.6% baseline (F2), within the GPU-wedge plan (no wedges, cooldown fires as configured).
4. GET /slots router 500s reduce (target router:500 == 0 per F3) and slots_stale drops.
5. Full project test suite passes; no regressions; metrics validated by re-running the F1 harness + F4 metric module.
